🇲🇽🚆 FIRST 12 LOCOMOTIVES ARRIVE FOR THE TREN MAYA DE CARGA

'A great piece of news — the first 12 locomotives of the freight Tren Maya have already arrived, and it's making very important progress,' Sheinbaum announced. The line will haul fuel, food, cement and containers across roughly 1,500 km of the Yucatán Peninsula, linking five southeastern states to Puerto Progreso and the Interoceanic Corridor. Inauguration set for 2027. The train they swore would never move a thing is about to move the southeast's economy.

🇲🇽🍎 UNICEF SINGLES OUT MEXICO AS GLOBAL CHILD OBESITY OVERTAKES HUNGER

The same week UNICEF reported that — for the first time in history — more of the world's children are obese than underweight, it praised Mexico by name: the 4T's ban on junk food and sugary drinks in every public school now shields 34 million students, in a country where ultra-processed products make up 40% of what a child eats each day. Treated as public policy, not personal failure — and not a market left to Coca-Cola.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>MEXICO'S SHARE OF US AUTO IMPORTS HITS LOWEST SINCE 2019 — AND EXPORTS DIVERSIFY</u>

El Economista reports Mexico's share of US light-vehicle imports fell to 19.2% in Jan–May 2026, the lowest since 2019, as Trump's 25% Section 232 tariffs bite. The flip side in the same data: the US now takes 75.4% of Mexican auto exports, down from 80.9% a year earlier — dependence on a single market is loosening under pressure.

🇲🇽⚽ <u>CDMX POSTS BIGGEST MONTHLY JOB GAIN IN OVER 20 YEARS ON WORLD CUP BOOM</u>

Mexico City created 100,756 formal jobs in June 2026 — its largest monthly formal-employment gain in more than two decades — powered by hosting the World Cup, per IMSS data. Mayor Clara Brugada put the tournament's economic spillover as high as 66 billion pesos, spread across all 16 boroughs in services, commerce, transport and tourism.

🇲🇽🚆 <u>THE LAWFARE MACHINE AGAINST THE MAYA TRAIN — 70 CASES KEPT ALIVE FOR YEARS</u>

A Contralínea investigation maps 70 environmental inspection cases still open against the Tren Maya — 24 on trunk-line sections — many stretched out up to five years since the last administration. The complainants read like a who's-who of the opposition: law firms tied to Claudio X. González, his Mexicans Against Corruption, Sélvame del Tren, and Julia Carabias. Profepa insists it "is not sabotaging the Tren Maya" — even as the expedientes stay conveniently open.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>INAI OFFICIALS SHOOK DOWN THE FOOTBALL FEDERATION — SHEINBAUM WANTS THEM SANCTIONED</u>

Leaked audio ties former commissioners of INAI — the "autonomous" transparency body sold for years as a democratic safeguard — to a shakedown of Mexico's football federation: flag data-privacy violations, then hint the fines soften if the Femexfut hires an "allied" law firm, plus three World Cup opening-ceremony tickets each. Sheinbaum's line on the officials who did it: they "must be sanctioned."

🇲🇽📊 <u>PEW: MEXICANS SOUR ON THE ECONOMY, STILL BACK SHEINBAUM TO RUN IT</u>

Pew Research finds 49% of Mexicans call the economy good, down from 61% a year ago after a Q1 contraction. Yet in the same poll, 61% approve of how Sheinbaum manages the economy, 65% back her on education, and 55% on her handling of the United States.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>US BLAMES MEXICAN LETTUCE FOR TACO BELL OUTBREAK — ORIGIN STILL UNCONFIRMED</u>

A cyclospora outbreak that sickened more than 1,664 Americans and hospitalized 94 across five US states has Washington's health agencies pointing at Mexican iceberg lettuce from Guanajuato. Mexico's Health Secretariat won't rubber-stamp it: "no se ha definido el origen" — the source has not been established. The lettuce was packed and distributed by Taylor Farms, a US company.

🇲🇽⚽ Sheinbaum will attend the World Cup final in New Jersey — on a booked commercial ticket. "I received an invitation from President Trump to go to the World Cup final on Sunday, and I made the decision to attend." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, July 18 Argentina vs. Spain at MetLife Stadium. Mexico co-hosted the 2026 World Cup alongside the US and Canada. Sheinbaum flies out Saturday night and returns Monday — no presidential jet, a commercial seat. The trip lands days before the third round of USMCA review talks.
